steps.body: Ten single ones bundle together to make one ten. A "ten" is just 10 ones grouped into a rod. So 3 tens is the same as 30 ones — three groups of ten.
Build it with blocks — rods are tens, cubes are ones.

widget.prompt: Build 30 any way you like — all rods, rods and cubes, whatever lands on 30.

commonBuilds.feedback: That's 33 — the 3 cubes add 3 more. Thirty is three rods with NO extra cubes, or a trade like 2 rods and 10 cubes.
3 cubes make 3, not 30. A rod is worth ten cubes — thirty needs three rods' worth, one way or another.

widget.missFeedback: Count by tens for the rods, then by ones for the cubes — the total must land exactly on 30.
widget.successFeedback: 30! Three rods, or 2 rods and 10 cubes, or 1 rod and 20 cubes — every trade of 1 rod for 10 cubes keeps the amount the same. That trade is what a ten IS.

predict.prompt: Maya builds 30 with 3 rods. Leo builds it with 2 rods and 10 cubes. Who has more?
predict.reveal: A rod IS ten cubes bundled together, so trading 1 rod for 10 cubes changes the look but never the amount — both builds are exactly 30.

cml.actionGoal: Exchange ten ones for one ten and prove that the represented number is unchanged.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: Create a second build for the same number using one more ten and ten fewer ones.

explanation.prompt: Why is one ten interchangeable with ten ones?

options.label: Both representations have a value of ten.
options.feedback: Exactly. Unit value, not visual size, makes one ten equal to ten ones.

options.label: A ten is larger because it is drawn longer.
options.feedback: That describes a surface feature, not the mathematical relationship that must remain true. Unit value, not visual size, makes one ten equal to ten ones.

explanationVariants: Each ten is 10 ones, so five tens make 50 ones.

widget.prompt: How many ones are the same as 5 tens?

commonErrors.feedback: 5 is the number of tens. Each ten is 10 ones, so 5 tens = 50 ones.

steps.body: Going the other way, 40 ones make 4 tens, because 40 is 4 groups of ten. To find how many tens, count the groups of ten.
Build the tens instead of entering a count.

widget.prompt: Build 40 in standard form with tens rods and ones cubes.

commonBuilds.feedback: Four rods and four cubes make 44. Forty has no extra ones.
Four cubes make 4. Forty needs four groups of ten.

widget.missFeedback: Use four tens rods and no ones cubes.
widget.successFeedback: Four tens and zero ones make 40.

steps.body: A bundle keeps its size: 1 ten is always 10 ones, whether you see a rod or ten loose cubes. Bundling into tens makes big counts quick to read.

commonErrors.feedback: 70 is the number of ones. It takes 7 groups of ten to make 70, so 7 tens.
70 splits into 7 groups of ten, so 7 tens.

explanationVariants: 60 ones grouped into tens is 6 tens.
Every ten ones make 1 ten: 60 ones = 6 tens.

widget.prompt: How many tens are the same as 60 ones?

commonErrors.feedback: 60 is the number of ones given, not the number of tens. Every ten ones is 1 ten, so 60 ones = 6 tens.
That mixes the digits together. Group 60 ones into tens: 60 ones = 6 tens.

explanationVariants: 20 apples grouped into bags of ten is 2 bags.
It takes 2 bags of ten to pack 20 apples.

widget.prompt: Apples are packed in bags of ten. There are 20 apples. How many bags are full?

commonErrors.feedback: 20 is the number of apples, not the number of bags. 20 apples packed in tens make 2 full bags.
That mixes the digits together. 20 apples split into groups of ten make 2 bags.

widget.fallbackFeedback: 20 apples packed in bags of ten make 2 full bags.

explanationVariants: 9 bundles of ten straws is 9 × 10 = 90 straws.
Each bundle is 10 straws, so nine bundles make 90 straws.

widget.prompt: A classroom counts out 9 bundles of ten straws. How many straws is that in all?

commonErrors.feedback: 9 is the number of bundles, not the total straws. Each bundle is 10 straws, so 9 bundles = 90 straws.
Don't just join the digits — 9 bundles of ten straws make 90 straws.

widget.fallbackFeedback: 9 bundles of ten straws make 90 straws.

hints: Each bundle of ten is 10 straws.
So count by tens: 10, 20, 30, … nine times.

steps.body: Ten ones make a ten, and you can bundle or unbundle.
takeaways: To turn tens into ones, count by tens.
To find tens, count the groups of ten.
steps.teaser: next: the tens and ones inside a two-digit number.

concept.body: One ten is 10 ones bundled together. So 3 tens = 30 ones (count by tens), and 40 ones = 4 tens (count the groups of ten).

widget.prompt: How many ones are the same as 3 tens?

commonErrors.feedback: Each ten is 10 ones, so 3 tens = 30 ones.
